code:
Producer sends, doesn't retry:
  send() fails -> event never arrives -> gone, no retry

Consumer commits before processing:
  commit() -> [crash] -> handle() never ran -> silently lost
caption: Cheapest option — a legitimate choice for loss-tolerant data.

code:
Producer retries until acked:
  send() -> ack lost in transit -> retry -> written twice

Consumer commits after handle() succeeds:
  handle() succeeds -> [crash before commit] -> re-processed
caption: Never silently loses data — duplicates are the trade-off, and the common default.

code:
Idempotent producer:
  retry w/ same producer ID + sequence number
  -> broker recognizes it, discards the duplicate

Transaction (read -> process -> write):
  offset commit + downstream write succeed together, or both roll back
caption: Genuine, but only covers the Kafka-to-Kafka hop, with real overhead.
